hypothesis: If the claim holds, nearly all sizeable oceanic islands will have at least one native bat species, and remote ones will often hold endemic bats.
pass_criterion: At least 80% of oceanic islands >100 km2 have >= 1 native bat species in IUCN ranges, and at least 30% of those more than 1000 km from a continent have >= 1 endemic bat.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of the oceanic islands have a native bat, or fewer than 10% of the remote ones have an endemic bat.
interpretation: 'Ærial mammals' means Chiroptera. 'Almost every island' is read as >= 80% of oceanic islands above a minimum size. The size limit is added to avoid tiny islets for which range maps cannot resolve presence.

dataset.name: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species - Mammals spatial data (Chiroptera)
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: Chiroptera range polygons, presence/origin codes and endemic status, overlaid on island polygons.
